preference_learning.purpose: Use explicit user-selected articles only as positive examples of desired content themes, workflow depth, tools and production value. The source website or domain of a sample is provenance only and must not become a preferred source.
preference_learning.ranking_policy: Similarity to the content semantics of positive samples may increase user_interest_fit, but source-domain similarity must contribute zero preference weight. Positive samples must never bypass source verification, Published Intelligence Registry canonical URL dedupe, substantive-delta checks, classification, Quality Gate, Full Analysis depth, release gates or category diversity.
preference_learning.sample_source_policy: Positive-sample URLs exist only to identify the examples and preserve provenance. Do not convert their hostnames, publishers or domains into source boosts, required checks, site-specific quotas or targeted site scans.
derived_content_signals: end-to-end character production breakdown from concept to final asset
practical reproducible material or shader tutorial
production-useful DCC tool or add-on solving a concrete workflow problem
high-value hand-keyed or stylized animation reference
stylized character presentation with strong animation or visual-development reference
artist-authored workflow breakdown with concrete modeling, texturing, rigging, animation or rendering decisions

source_neutrality.discovery_policy: Expand queries from topics, tools, techniques, workflow stages and production problems represented by preference samples. Search across heterogeneous verifiable sources; never constrain or bias discovery toward the domains that hosted the samples.
source_neutrality.ranking_policy: Rank source reliability on evidence quality and verifiability. Publisher/domain identity may affect reliability assessment when independently justified, but must not receive preference affinity merely because that domain hosted a user-selected sample.

discovery_source_pool.policy: Explicitly registered websites are discovery channels only. Registration allows active candidate discovery from the site but gives zero preference/ranking bonus, creates no quota, and does not bypass verification, dedupe, substantive-delta, Quality Gate, FULL/BRIEF/REJECT classification or source-diversity rules.

sources.name: 80 Level
sources.notes: Use 80 Level as one heterogeneous discovery channel for production breakdowns, tools, tutorials, animation, engine art and emerging 3D/AI work. Do not treat it as a preferred publisher and do not require a daily hit.

sources.name: 3D人 / 3DNchu
sources.notes: Japanese CG discovery source with frequent coverage of 3D/2D/VR/game/AI tools, Blender add-ons, engine projects and technical releases. Treat linked primary sources as preferred verification evidence when available.

sources.name: CGWORLD.jp
sources.notes: Japanese professional CG and VFX publication. Use for studio production breakdowns, character/environment/animation workflows, engine and DCC techniques, interviews and technical case studies.

sources.name: Bilibili
sources.notes: Video discovery source for reproducible tutorials, demonstrations, rigging/animation education, engine art, DCC workflows and AI 3D tests. Creator claims require corroboration when production-impact claims extend beyond the demonstrated evidence.

sources.name: ArtStation
sources.notes: Artist and studio portfolio discovery source. Prioritize posts containing concrete breakdowns, WIP, modeling/texturing/material/lighting/animation decisions or technical workflow evidence; pure portfolio images without useful production detail may be reference-only or rejected.

sources.name: Gumroad Discover
sources.notes: Marketplace discovery source for DCC add-ons, scripts, materials, rigs, brushes, production tools and educational resources. Marketplace copy is candidate evidence only; prefer author documentation, demos, changelogs, GitHub or other primary technical evidence when validating concrete capabilities and production impact.

sources.name: Xiaohongshu / RED
sources.notes: Social discovery source for creator-authored tutorials, workflow notes, tool tests, DCC/engine tips, AI 3D experiments and production references. Treat posts as candidate evidence only; concrete technical or production-impact claims should be corroborated with reproducible demonstrations, author primary material, official documentation or other independent evidence when possible.

3d-animation.purpose: Broaden animation intelligence beyond AI motion and tool news to include durable fundamentals and production-ready rigging education.
content_mix: mocap, cleanup, retarget and facial animation
fundamental_animation_topics: weight, balance and center of gravity
walk, run, idle, attack and locomotion cycles
pose readability, silhouette and line of action
source_preferences: official DCC or engine documentation and training
experienced animator or rigging educator tutorials
GDC, SIGGRAPH or reputable training material
3d-animation.tutorial_policy: High-quality foundational tutorials are valid production intelligence even when evergreen or beginner-accessible. Favor reproducible teaching, strong visual explanation and direct production transfer; do not require a new product announcement.
3d-animation.freshness_policy: Fresh material wins when quality is comparable, but strong 1-6 month and evergreen keypose, body-mechanics and rigging tutorials remain eligible.
3d-animation.diversity_guard: Tutorials enrich discovery and ranking but never create a per-topic quota. Avoid allowing one DCC, one educator, one publisher or one tutorial theme to dominate the category.
